title: Family seeking answers
article: Gordon Walker Bowe's family is seeking answers after his death in Calgary on Nov. 2.
The father of Bowe's common law wife, John Chernenkoff, said what is known is Bowe spoke to a friend at 7:48 p.m. on Nov. 1.
The friend told an Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) special investigator that Bowe sounded normal and was looking forward to getting home.
"The details of what happened between 7:48 and 8:15 p.m. when the police were called are sketchy at best," said John.
He said Bowe was seen running, trying to hide from someone, Bowe sought and found refuge in the basement of a vacant house.
At 8:15 p.m., neighbours heard the sound of glass breaking and called the police, said John.
"It is unclear if the breaking glass was caused by Gordon or by someone trying to gain access to him in the basement," said John.
"From the evidence (the family) has seen at the house we suspect it was the latter," John said.
John said Gordon was barefoot and if he had broken the window he would have cuts on the bottom of his feet, but he didn't.
The family believes Bowe gained access to the house through a side door, which he locked behind him and the glass was broken later.
John was told by one of the investigators that when police first arrived on the scene Bowe was, "co-operative and submissive."

"What happened between then and when he arrived at the hospital we can only suspect. The crime scene however remains unsecured and evidence is deteriorating. This fact alone does not instill confidence that all the truth of what transpired will ever be known," said Chernenkoff.
Zoya Chernenkoff, Bowe's common law wife, said once she heard the news, she did not know what to think.
"Once I got there and saw the evidence myself I think he was brutally beaten ..." Zoya said
John said the medical examiner told the family the taser had nothing to do with Bowe's death.
"In this case, Gordon's whole side was swollen, his neck and face were bruised," John said.
John said the family has no faith in the ASIRT team heading the investigation into Bowe's death.
Zoya said she won't stop fighting until she gets to the truth.
ASIRT executive director Clif Purvis could not comment on anything the family said and added the matter is still under investigation.
John Dooks with the The Calgary Police Association did not return the Castlegar New's phone call before the deadline.
